clue.text: 20 shillings, cents or euros?

parts.note: s. was the old abbreviation for a shilling
c is the usual abbreviation for cents
taken as written
E is short for euros

explanation.surface: A puzzle about converting money: what would twenty old shillings come to in cents or euros?
explanation.walkthrough: Twenty shillings made a pound in Britain's old money, so the surface invites a currency sum; the number itself is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a set of twenty, an old counting word for that number.

clue.text: Forced to leave prune?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: drove away, saw a rival off
second meaning: cut away a branch with a blade

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a prune being expelled; read the first part as a past tense phrase and the second as a gardening verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To see off someone is to defeat or repel them, and its past tense pairs with removing a limb using a toothed blade.

clue.text: Work in China for US?

parts.note: surface reading: some job or project being done in China on behalf of America; setter's reading: China is rhyming slang for mate, so a mate belonging to us both, the title of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: An American contract being carried out in China.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so 'china' is a friend; a friend shared by us is a friend in common. The capital-letter US hides the plain pronoun us.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the title of Charles Dickens's last completed novel, a literary piece of writing.

clue.text: Standards maintained by internet hosting

indicators.note: what is maintained by the following words is held inside them, so look within the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Rules about acceptable standards upheld by a web hosting company.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the guiding set of values and principles of a group, its moral code.

clue.text: Marine guide possibly working for island

indicators.note: working letters are put into action and moved about, so rearrange the phrase

parts.note: the two words supply all the letters

explanation.surface: A sea guide who also works on behalf of an island community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine guide' reads like a person showing tourists round; it is the part of a fish that keeps it steady and on course.
explanation.definitionFit: The back fin of a fish or dolphin stabilises it and helps steer through water, hence a guide in the sea.

clue.text: Daughter opens robe in fantastic scene

parts.note: d is the standard abbreviation for daughter
to ream is to widen or open out a hole
a cape is a sleeveless cloak or robe

explanation.surface: A girl unwraps a dressing gown in an elaborate stage set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opens' looks like the daughter beginning the word, but it is a verb of its own: reaming is enlarging a hole with a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamscape is an imagined, surreal landscape like one seen while sleeping.

clue.text: No introduction needed for gospel book

indicators.note: without an introduction the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: gospel means something absolutely true

explanation.surface: A gospel that is so well known it needs no preface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gospel book' reads as one phrase about the New Testament; gospel is the wordplay, and book alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a short book of the Old Testament telling of a Moabite widow.

clue.text: Greek hero soon captures willing maiden

indicators.note: to capture something is to hold it inside, so one piece surrounds the others

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
game means up for it, willing
M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A legendary Greek warrior is about to carry off a willing young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, written M on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the king of Mycenae who led the Greeks in the Trojan War.

clue.text: Officer left in tears, unit disbanded

indicators.note: a disbanded group is broken up and scattered, so the letters are dispersed and regrouped

parts.note: every letter of these words is used

clue.text: Good to admit oxygen can poison

parts.note: nice is a mild synonym of good
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a can of oxygen might be useful as a poison antidote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb meaning is able to; it is the container noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotine, the tobacco alkaloid, is toxic in high doses and was used as an insecticide.

clue.text: Best time to run in defeat

indicators.note: the preceding pieces are placed inside the word that follows

parts.note: to worst someone is to beat them
t is the abbreviation for time
hie is an old verb meaning hurry

explanation.surface: The ideal moment to flee during a rout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defeat' looks like a noun but is the verb worst, meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: The most worthy is the most deserving or excellent, the superlative of a word for admirable.

clue.text: Golden arches — usual rubbish is consumed, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the leading letter of each word

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: The famous golden arches of a fast-food chain, where the usual junk food is eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Auric is the adjective from the Latin for gold, describing gold or its compounds.

clue.text: Perhaps those in rubber will excite more of us

definitions.note: the answer is the group as a whole, a singular noun

indicators.note: exciting something stirs it up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: the three words supply all the letters

explanation.surface: A cheeky suggestion that people dressed in rubber will arouse the rest of us.
explanation.walkthrough: A rubber is a match in bridge, played by four people, which the surface hides behind a racier reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge rubber is played by two pairs, a group of four players.

clue.text: Go about as a bird would go!

clue.text: Result of zero fare? A motorhome to take Channel crossing

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price; here it is food, and 'Channel' is a TV station, not the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no food at all leads to severe hunger and wasting away.

clue.text: Liquid runs so if retaining "A", "X" being liquid property

indicators.note: retaining is holding inside, so the rearranged letters wrap round the rest
something liquid flows and has no fixed shape, so the letters run into a new order

parts.note: the three words supply the letters to be rearranged
A stands for ace on playing cards
X is ten in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A puzzling physics instruction about how a liquid behaves when it holds certain symbols.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid' appears twice: first it signals the rearrangement, and only the second use belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the elastic tendency of a fluid's outer layer to resist an external force, a physical characteristic of fluids.

clue.text: Coast, where waves seem to gather?

indicators.note: gathering is drawing something in, so the outer word takes the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: to feel, as in it feels odd, is to seem

indicators.note: waves move letters to and fro, so the word before is rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaside riddle: the shore is where the breakers appear to collect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coast' reads as the seashore and 'waves' as the sea; coast is a verb meaning roll along without pedalling.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to move without power, as a cyclist does when not pedalling down a slope.

clue.text: Physicist's worry over traveller

explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' in a down clue puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Anders Ångström was a Swedish physicist, a pioneer of spectroscopy whose name is given to a tiny unit of length.

clue.text: Keep going to Latin classes

clue.text: Run out of clothes?

clue.text: Lounge lizard initially bends over

parts.note: the first letter of lizard

clue.text: Ready for battle
